blocks.text: The ‘head’ is composed of the prostomium, peristomium, and, in some cases, anterior segments (Fig. 2.2). The prostomium contains at least part of the brain, and often has eyes, antennae, and palps. Prostomia vary a great deal in shape from conical semi-spherical, T-shaped structures, to elongate lobes that or extend back along the body. In many taxa the peristomium is one (e.g. Arenicolidae, Cossura, Scalibregmatidae, Sabellidae), or two (e.g. Eunicidae) com- plete rings separating the prostomium from the first segment (Figs. 2.2b, c, d, e, f, j). In taxa such as Acrocirridae and Spionidae, the peristomium may be difficult to see dorsally, but still appears to form a ring (Fig. 2.2d). blocks.text: Head appendages include antennae, palps, peristomial cirri, and, associated with one or more cephalized segments, anterior dor- sal cirri. Antennae are always located on the prostomium. Up to three antennae may be present, including a pair of lateral anten- nae and one median antenna (Figs. 2.2a, b, i, k).
